cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and the adjusting is yours and deliberate.
cells.act: keep the ritual and give it room to change
cells.ask: Take a habit you keep with the people you tend and alter a single piece of it this week — the rest stays — then notice how they come in.
cells.core:
When you're tending something that isn't finished yet, you can hold several readings of it at once and still stay easy in your own skin. What a person needs today and not last week, the temperature of a gathering, the small correction that keeps something alive rather than frozen — you feel for those and move with them, and it doesn't scatter you. What you adjust stays in its own shape.

A habit you keep with the people you tend, some way of marking a thing — take it up this week and alter a single piece of it. Keep the rest; don't rebuild it. Notice how they come in after that. A practice you can adjust is one you're still holding; a practice nobody's allowed to touch is one that's holding you. What they do at the threshold tells you which it is.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the thing alive by adjusting it as it grows.
cells.verb: sensing when to add, when to take away, and how to blend
cells.place: beside what is still growing, tended and not hurried

cells.tense: You will have smoothed the next rough thing before it can arrive.
cells.act: go where the feeling is already pulling
cells.ask: Follow the pull you keep talking yourself out of — one step toward it today, no plan past that step — and see where you land.
cells.core:
You can read what a gathering is about to do before it does it, and lately you've been using that to get the smoothing in early. In the places you tend, disagreements get resolved at the speed of a good host; the harder thing gets folded away before anyone can look at it. It reads as calm. It's a forecast you're proud of, and the forecast has started to matter more than the people standing in it.

Something is pulling at you here, and you've been talking yourself out of it. Follow that pull today — one step, no plan past that step. Don't bring it down to size first. The calm you've been keeping will get a little thinner, and what's underneath gets to be worked with. That's the direction, and it only asks one step toward what you already feel.
cells.sheetLine: You smooth things before they get to be true.

cells.tense: You kept a room steady back there, and that room is behind you now.
cells.act: sit with someone in it without fixing it
cells.ask: Sit with one person while they're in it and do nothing about it — no adjusting, no lightening, no solution handed over — and stay until you leave.
cells.core:
In the places you tend, the ground was steady once and it isn't now. Things you used to hold whole come apart while you're handling them; each person you look after pulls a different part of the day loose, and there's no centre left to adjust from. You're still watching for the moment to step in. The adjusting hasn't stopped. There's just less of you arriving in it.

Caring for something isn't only making it easier. Sit with one person while they're in it and do nothing about it. No adjusting, no lightening, no solution handed over. Stay until you leave. Letting what they're carrying reach you is the part that puts you back into your own day — and it's allowed to be imperfect. Once is enough, in whatever shape is available to you.
cells.sheetLine: You still adjust for others, with less of you arriving to do it.

cells.tense: You are integrating without knowing it, pen down in a room you've already written.
cells.act: learn how the people before you did it
cells.ask: Ask the person who tended this before you how they did it, and listen — keep what's yours, let what's theirs stay theirs.
cells.core:
The adjusting is already happening through you — you shift the pacing of a meal so a person doesn't have to say anything, hand back a worry at a size they can carry — and if anyone asked, you'd call it having a good eye. The doing is real. Where it came from isn't anywhere you've kept it. You've been running this as instinct, and the account of how you got it exists only in other people's memories.

Something you do with the people you tend came from someone — taught to you, or borrowed without noticing. Ask whoever tended before you how they did it. Then pass what you got from them on to somebody younger, with one change of your own folded in. That's the move that puts the name back on it. You keep what's yours; you hear where it came from, and one person after you gets to hold it too.

attempts.check: The draft's weakest claim is that the person's tuning is 'for' the people they tend; the record shows the capacity, not its object, so I'll say what the tuning does in moments they'd recognise and leave the direction open. A reader could rightly say their adjusting is just how they run a room, not care — the asks survive that because each is one visible act that teaches something regardless of motive. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line about what their adjusting costs them; I'll keep to what it makes visible.
